key_insight: Phase change couples with inertia and gravity to intensify cloud-droplet preferential concentration by creating size-dependent settling differences along droplet trajectories.
engineering_relevance: This matters for cloud microphysics modeling because altered droplet clustering can change collision and coalescence rates, affecting precipitation formation predictions.
method: Developed an analytical theory for concentration changes in inertial droplets with gravity and phase change.
Decomposed preferential concentration into contributions from settling, droplet transport, and fluid deformation.
Applied the theory to 2D homogeneous thermal convection simulations.
evidence_signal: In the convection simulations, phase change markedly increased preferential concentration, with the strongest effect coming from spatially varying settling speeds caused by different thermodynamic histories.
watch_item: The enhancement is scale-dependent: fluid deformation can thin clustering structures and reduce the measured concentration at a fixed spatial resolution.
paper_title: Preferential concentration of cloud droplets: Coupled effects of phase change and gravitational settling
